title: Industry 4.0
sub: Seminar 8 · the four industrial revolutions and the 17 technologies of Industry 4.0
blurb: The four revolutions in one line each, and all 17 technologies: what they are and one real example, from your own Team O workshop sheet.
lede: Practice Test 2 asks you to explain each of the 17 technologies and give one manufacturing example. The descriptions here come from the seminar slides; the examples come from your own team's workshop sheet.
six: Four revolutions: **1784 steam** (UK) · **1870 electricity** · **1969 electronics** (the microchip) · **Industry 4.0 connectivity**.
**Industry 4.0** (i4.0): a German concept from **2012**, the Internet of Things applied to industry (IIoT).
The Czech Academy of Sciences lists **17 technologies** related to Industry 4.0.
In the test: **explain** each technology and give **one example** in manufacturing.
As a manager you don't need to be an engineer, but you must judge whether a technology makes sense, financially too.
foot: Sources: 3BE216 seminar slides 'Industry 4.0' (descriptions), your Team O workshop sheet (examples), Seminar 8 as recorded.

questions.answer: a German concept from 2012: connectivity, the Internet of Things applied to industry

facts: The first industrial revolution started in {1784|1870|1969|2012}.

Industry 4.0 started as a German concept in {2012|1784|1969|2000}.
Plants used as sensors are called {biosensors|new sensors|terahertz|graphene}.
